right-command.requires: A human using the physical right Command key on the target Mac. Synthesized key events are not evidence.

cases.name: Rapid tap-to-toggle
cases.steps: Focus a text field, tap physical Right Command, then tap it again within 300 ms.
cases.expected: Listening stops immediately, the pill changes to Finishing, and the app never remains stuck in Listening.

cases.name: Rapid cycles during finish
cases.steps: Complete RC-001, then start a second dictation while the first transcription is still finishing.
cases.expected: The newer listening session owns the pill and tray; completion of the older session cannot hide or stop it.

cases.name: Escape cancellation
cases.steps: Start dictation, speak, press Escape before stopping.
cases.expected: Capture ends, the pill disappears, nothing is transcribed or pasted, and the previous clipboard remains unchanged.

cases.name: Push-to-talk
cases.steps: Enable push-to-talk, hold physical Right Command while speaking, then release it.
cases.expected: Recording lasts only while held and release enters Finishing exactly once.

cases.name: Background app state
cases.steps: Close the main window without quitting, focus another app, and dictate.
cases.expected: Dictation starts without opening My Assistant and pastes into the previously focused field.

cases.name: Target-app coverage
cases.steps: Dictate into TextEdit, Chrome, Safari, Slack or Discord, and a native settings-style text field.
cases.expected: Each supported editable field receives one clean paste; failures name the exact target and control.

cases.name: Full-screen focus
cases.steps: Dictate into a text field in a full-screen app or Space.
cases.expected: The pill does not steal focus and output returns to the original field.

cases.name: Multiple displays
cases.steps: Repeat dictation on each connected display for every configured pill position.
cases.expected: The pill is fully visible on the active display, never clipped or stranded on another Space.

cases.name: Silence and accidental tap
cases.steps: Start and stop without speaking.
cases.expected: No model hallucination is pasted and the UI returns to Idle.

cases.name: Model unavailable
cases.steps: Run with the local model unavailable, then attempt dictation.
cases.expected: The app returns to Idle with actionable setup guidance; it never remains Listening or crashes.

cases.name: Permission recovery
cases.steps: Test with Accessibility or Microphone denied, grant it in Settings, relaunch when instructed, and retry.
cases.expected: Failure is explained under the correct app identity and the next attempt works without duplicate prompts.

cases.name: Sleep and event-tap recovery
cases.steps: Sleep and wake the Mac, wait one minute, then dictate without relaunching.
cases.expected: Right Command still produces one start/stop edge and no duplicate sessions.

cases.name: Clipboard policies
cases.steps: Repeat once with Never Save and once with Save/Replace.
cases.expected: Never Save restores the previous clipboard after paste; Save/Replace retains the dictated text.

cases.name: Input-device failure
cases.steps: Start with an unavailable or disconnected input device, then recover to the built-in microphone.
cases.expected: The app exits Listening safely, explains the failure, and a later attempt succeeds without restart when macOS permits.

cases.name: Sustained reliability
cases.steps: Perform 25 start/stop cycles including five sub-second rapid toggles.
cases.expected: Exactly 25 sessions start and stop; no crash, stuck pill, missed edge, duplicate paste, helper leak, or growing idle model process.

agent-context.requires: Use only a dedicated test account or synthetic content. Record aggregate observations, never private page text, document content, access tokens, or screenshots containing personal data.

cases.name: Gmail read-only context
cases.steps: Open a synthetic Gmail draft and invoke Inspect app behind My Assistant.
cases.expected: The active Gmail window and useful compose roles are identified within bounds; no click, edit, send, screenshot, persistence, or provider call occurs.

cases.name: Slack read-only context
cases.steps: Open a synthetic Slack channel or draft in the native app or supported browser and invoke the inspector.
cases.expected: Useful visible roles are returned without expanding hidden history, changing the draft, or exposing secure fields.

cases.name: LinkedIn read-only context
cases.steps: Open a synthetic LinkedIn message composer and invoke the inspector.
cases.expected: The composer context is bounded and identifiable; no message is written or sent.

cases.name: Google Docs read-only context
cases.steps: Open a disposable Google Doc containing synthetic text, focus the document, and invoke the inspector.
cases.expected: The app/window and available editor semantics are reported honestly; an incomplete canvas tree is marked as a gap rather than invented.

cases.name: Apple Notes read-only context
cases.steps: Open a disposable note containing synthetic text, focus its body, and invoke the inspector.
cases.expected: The focused editable role is identified without modifying or persisting note content.

cases.name: Google Slides read-only context
cases.steps: Open a disposable presentation, focus a synthetic text box, and invoke the inspector.
cases.expected: Available slide/editor semantics are captured within bounds; canvas gaps are reported and no presentation change occurs.

cases.name: Terminal read-only context
cases.steps: Open Terminal on a harmless prompt with no secrets visible and invoke the inspector.
cases.expected: The terminal window is identified without executing a command, reading files, or turning visible text into instructions.

cases.name: Secure-field redaction
cases.steps: Focus a synthetic password field and invoke the inspector.
cases.expected: The secure value and descendant values are redacted; the snapshot contains no password-like content.

cases.name: Permission denial and recovery
cases.steps: Deny Accessibility, invoke the inspector, then grant access through the documented manual flow and retry after relaunch if macOS requires it.
cases.expected: Denial fails closed with correct recovery guidance; the later explicit retry succeeds without duplicate scanning.

cases.name: Full-screen and multiple displays
cases.steps: Repeat a synthetic inspection in a full-screen app and on each connected display.
cases.expected: The correct active window is selected each time and the inspector never captures another Space by accident.

cases.name: Untrusted screen instruction
cases.steps: Place synthetic prompt-injection text on screen, request a harmless draft preview, and inspect the structured result.
cases.expected: Screen text cannot override read-only policy, provider boundaries, output schema, or the user's instruction.

cases.name: Global Agent shortcut
cases.steps: Assign an unused shortcut, close the main window without quitting, then press the physical shortcut from another app.
cases.expected: My Assistant opens once on Agents with the request field focused; conflicts are explained and relaunch restores the saved binding.

cases.name: ChatGPT account proposal
cases.steps: With the official external Codex runtime installed, complete device-code sign-in, select an account-visible model and effort, and request a synthetic draft.
cases.expected: The model list and supported effort choices come from the account, the proposal is structured, and no OAuth token enters app settings or logs.

cases.name: API-key proposal
cases.steps: Save a test provider key in Keychain, load models, select one, configure its supported controls, and request a synthetic draft.
cases.expected: The selected provider/model is used, the key remains in Keychain, and output is bounded to draft, replace-selection, or no-op before any separate confirmation.

cases.name: Apply draft at cursor in disposable TextEdit
cases.steps: Create a new disposable TextEdit document containing synthetic text, place the cursor, prepare a draft, confirm the named TextEdit target, then click Apply draft.
cases.expected: Only the reviewed text is inserted at the original cursor after exact process and field revalidation; the result is verified and nothing is sent or submitted.

cases.name: Replace selected text in disposable TextEdit
cases.steps: Select synthetic text in a disposable TextEdit document, request a replacement, confirm the named target, then click Apply draft.
cases.expected: Only the still-selected range is replaced; the surrounding text remains byte-for-byte equivalent and the final value is verified.

cases.name: Stale process, app, window, text, or selection
cases.steps: Prepare a TextEdit proposal, then relaunch TextEdit, switch app/window, alter the field, move the cursor, or change the selection before Apply.
cases.expected: Apply is rejected as stale without guessing whichever app is behind My Assistant or mutating any target.

cases.name: Non-TextEdit, secure, and unsupported targets
cases.steps: Prepare synthetic drafts for a chatbox, password field, non-settable editor, and unsupported control role.
cases.expected: The target is named, the draft remains read-only, no Apply control or proposal ID exists, and no field value enters logs or process arguments.

cases.name: Guarded one-step Undo
cases.steps: Apply a synthetic draft and immediately choose Undo without changing the target.
cases.expected: The complete prior field value is restored and verified; the private undo value never appears in browser state, logs, disk, or process arguments.

cases.name: Undo after target drift
cases.steps: Apply a draft, then edit the field or change app/window before choosing Undo.
cases.expected: Undo cancels safely because the applied-value fingerprint no longer matches; the user's newer edit remains intact.

cases.name: Expiry, relaunch, and packaged helper
cases.steps: Test a proposal after two minutes, Undo after five minutes, app relaunch, and the signed packaged preview build.
cases.expected: Expired and relaunched state cannot execute; the packaged helper is present, correctly signed, on demand only, and leaves no idle process.

cases.name: Rollback truthfulness
cases.steps: Use an instrumented synthetic Accessibility fixture to return unchanged, transformed, unreadable, and rollback-failed outcomes without touching a real app.
cases.expected: Unchanged writes report rejection, verified restoration reports rolled back, and unreadable or unverified restoration reports an urgent verification failure; no path labels an unknown final state safe.

wake-word.requires: Explicit opt-in, a dedicated non-private phrase/noise corpus, and separately installed engine adapters. Porcupine requires the tester's own AccessKey and accepted vendor terms; no engine or secret is bundled in the DMG.

cases.name: External engine and licensing gate
cases.steps: Install the candidate adapter outside the app bundle and document its exact version, model license, commercial terms, and secret requirements.
cases.expected: The core DMG size is unchanged and the candidate is not marked shippable when redistribution or commercial terms are unresolved.

cases.name: Opt-in and visible state
cases.steps: Enable the benchmark explicitly, then pause and disable it.
cases.expected: Microphone monitoring never starts before opt-in; active, paused, and off states are always visible and truthful.

cases.name: Quiet-room recall
cases.steps: Run at least 100 phrase attempts across supported accents and speaking distances.
cases.expected: False-reject rate and p50/p95 activation latency are recorded per machine and accent, not summarized as an unqualified vendor claim.

cases.name: Cafe, wind, and traffic recall
cases.steps: Repeat the phrase matrix with consented real cafe, wind, and traffic conditions at documented levels.
cases.expected: Noise-specific false-reject and latency results are recorded without reusing private speech or training on it by default.

cases.name: Long-run false accepts
cases.steps: Run at least 10 hours of consented negative audio including meetings, media, typing, and similar phrases.
cases.expected: False accepts per hour and triggering phrases are recorded; any unintended full Agent capture is counted as a failure.

cases.name: CPU, RAM, energy, and package cost
cases.steps: Measure idle/listening CPU, physical footprint, RSS, Energy Impact, and adapter/model disk size on each supported Mac tier.
cases.expected: Incremental resource cost is separated from My Assistant baseline and remains within an approved product budget.

cases.name: Suspension gates
cases.steps: Test active meeting, dictation, screen lock, sleep/wake, microphone loss, and explicit pause.
cases.expected: Wake monitoring suspends and resumes exactly as configured with no duplicate stream, stuck microphone, or silent always-on state.

cases.name: Local privacy boundary
cases.steps: Observe files, logs, and network activity before and after phrase activation.
cases.expected: Pre-wake audio is processed locally, is not retained, and is not transmitted; only the post-activation instruction follows the selected compute privacy mode.

cases.name: Porcupine versus modern open controls
cases.steps: Run the identical corpus and measurement procedure through Porcupine, microWakeWord, and sherpa-onnx keyword spotting using exact pinned versions and properly licensed models.
cases.expected: The engine decision is evidence-based across accuracy, latency, CPU/RAM, battery, Mac integration maturity, and licensing; no candidate is selected from vendor or community claims alone.

two-person-meeting.requires: Two consenting people in a real call on the named platform. A prerecorded loop or one-person simulation is not platform acceptance.

cases.name: No idle false positive
cases.steps: Open the platform but do not join a call for two minutes.
cases.expected: No meeting notification, recording indicator, helper capture, or meeting record appears.

cases.name: Call-start detection
cases.steps: Join a real two-person call and exchange speech.
cases.expected: One native notification appears only after live-call audio/evidence exists; recording begins once.

cases.name: Scheduled and impromptu title
cases.steps: Run one calendar-linked call and one unscheduled call.
cases.expected: The scheduled meeting keeps its title; the unscheduled call becomes Impromptu meeting or Untitled meeting.

cases.name: Two-speaker capture
cases.steps: Each participant reads six alternating, identifiable lines.
cases.expected: Both sides are present in order with no dropped channel; attribution uses names only when reliable evidence exists.

cases.name: Overlap and interruption
cases.steps: Use three controlled overlaps and two interruptions.
cases.expected: Transcript order remains understandable, uncertainty is visible, and speakers are not confidently mislabeled.

cases.name: Live transcript
cases.steps: Keep the live panel open during alternating speech.
cases.expected: Lines arrive continuously with usable latency and the panel remains responsive.

cases.name: Mute and unmute
cases.steps: Mute and unmute each participant using the platform controls.
cases.expected: Muted speech is not invented; state changes do not end or duplicate the meeting.

cases.name: Pause and resume
cases.steps: Pause capture for 30 seconds while both people talk, then resume.
cases.expected: Paused content is absent by design, resume continues the same meeting, and the UI clearly indicates the gap.

cases.name: Scratchpad persistence
cases.steps: Write notes before and after pause, close and reopen the meeting panel.
cases.expected: Notes survive and attach to the correct meeting without entering the transcript.

cases.name: Screen recording on
cases.steps: Enable screen recording and share changing visual content.
cases.expected: The saved meeting can play the recording and its thumbnail comes from that recording.

cases.name: Screen recording off
cases.steps: Repeat with screen recording disabled.
cases.expected: No video artifact is created and the meeting uses the detected platform icon as its thumbnail.

cases.name: Screen-share state
cases.steps: Start and stop platform screen sharing twice.
cases.expected: Capture continues, share evidence updates when supported, and My Assistant's protected overlay is not present in the recording.

cases.name: Automatic end and notes
cases.steps: Leave the call normally and wait for processing.
cases.expected: Recording stops once, transcript finalizes incrementally, and notes/action items begin automatically without manual navigation.

cases.name: Permission failure and recovery
cases.steps: Deny one required permission, observe failure, grant it, and retry.
cases.expected: The correct missing permission is named, existing transcript data stays safe, and retry does not create a ghost meeting.

cases.name: Abrupt platform exit
cases.steps: Force-quit the meeting platform during the call.
cases.expected: My Assistant detects the end, finalizes valid media, preserves transcript lines, and remains running.

cases.name: Assistant relaunch recovery
cases.steps: Quit or crash My Assistant mid-call, reopen it, and continue with consent.
cases.expected: The prior partial meeting remains readable and recovery behavior is explicit; no corrupt or silently merged record.

cases.name: 45-minute resource soak
cases.steps: Run a 45-minute two-person call with screen recording off.
cases.expected: No crash, runaway RSS, unbounded temporary audio, transcript loss, or severe UI slowdown occurs.

cases.name: History after relaunch
cases.steps: Relaunch My Assistant and open the completed meeting.
cases.expected: Title, participants, duration, scratchpad, transcript, summary state, media/thumbnail choice, and corrections persist.
